title: 1981 AHSME Problem 20
statement: A ray of light originates from point \(A\) and travels in a plane, being reflected \(n\) times between lines \(AD\) and \(CD,\) before striking a point \(B\) (which may be on \(AD\) or \(CD\)) perpendicularly and retracing its path to \(A.\) (At each point of reflection the light makes two equal angles as indicated in the adjoining figure. The figure shows the light path for \(n=3.\)) If \(\angle CDA=8^\circ,\) what is the largest value \(n\) can have?

solutions.text:
Let \(\theta\gt0\) be the initial acute angle between the ray and \(AD.\) Successive exterior-angle relations increase the corresponding acute angle by \(8^\circ\) at each reflection. At the final perpendicular strike, \[ 90^\circ=\theta+(8n+8)^\circ. \] Thus \(\theta=82^\circ-8n^\circ\gt0,\) so \(n\lt\frac{82}{8}=10.25.\) The greatest integer possible is \(10,\) attained when \(\theta=2^\circ.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Track the acute angle between the ray and each successive reflecting line
Each reflection advances that angle by the wedge angle \(8^\circ\)
